891354fdf71c1ff1b9f5258c0ee3fc46575bf7f5.summary: Genians Security Center describes NodeLinkRAT, a JavaScript remote access tool run on a Node.js runtime, used in a June to October 2026 campaign against South Korean policy and security professionals. The attack began with reply-based spearphishing posing as a National Assembly member's aide, using a disguised shortcut file. Later stages were fetched from a public note service whose contents the operator swapped to change tools, including XenoRAT and document-theft scripts. GSC assesses the campaign as Kimsuky with moderate confidence.

hedges: GSC assesses the Kimsuky attribution with moderate confidence; no single decisive piece of evidence has been obtained.
XenoRAT is open source, and Dropbox and free hosting are commonly abused by many threat actors, so those alone carry limited weight.
A third party may have imitated the same techniques, and this cannot be completely ruled out.
Korean strings and South Korean services may reflect targeting of South Korea, and deliberate deception is also possible.
There may be attack stages that have not been identified, because the note page content changed frequently.
Victim-specific code may have been selected through another, unconfirmed method, which cannot be ruled out.

897859e26d8d826c960079ec86527a483bd77bda.summary: FinFisher RAT is a commercial spyware family, referred to in its listed reports also as FinSpy. It is known mainly as a full remote access trojan, used in governmental targeted and lawful criminal investigations. Reported features include password harvesting, anti-detection capabilities and use of VMProtect. The listed reports from 2014 to 2021 include a FireEye report on CVE-2017-8759, a zero-day used in the wild to distribute FINSPY, and Kaspersky Labs' report on BlackOasis APT attacks using a zero-day exploit.

89dc96ea163d64499eef809f5a13a6fb906ea27b.summary: ANSSI reports the Houken intrusion set, which exploited zero-day flaws in Ivanti Cloud Service Appliance devices from September 2024 to gain initial access to French government, telecoms, media, finance and transport organisations. ANSSI suspects Houken is run by the same threat actor as UNC5174, likely as an access broker selling footholds. It also observed one data exfiltration case and an interest in cryptomining. Attribution is hedged throughout the report.

894ee40df27ecc1c7eaa7bd6a2ca715ab62fc643.summary: Kaspersky Lab, as reported in the article, describes three cybercrime groups targeting banks in Russia with APT-style tactics. Metel automates the rollback of ATM transactions while emptying ATMs and was found inside 30 organizations. GCMAN stayed inside one bank's network for 18 months before moving money. Carbanak 2.0 has moved beyond banks to budgeting and accounting departments, and Carbanak was confirmed to be still active. Victim banks are not named because of an ongoing law enforcement investigation.
